Connections: a manifest may declare `connections:` entries: a name, a credential-free HTTPS `base_url` that passes SSRF checks, auth kind `none|bearer|header` and a pinned local OpenAPI file. bearer and header must also name an environment variable in `env` (review refuses the connection without it, but it is validated and not read: see Credentials), and header declares the header NAME in the manifest. External connections are active when enabled by the owner and authorized by the grant. The runtime validates these declarations and routes only to the pinned read contract.

External read tools: a tool with handler kind: external (connection, operation_id) and effect: read binds that connection and a reviewed `operation_id`; external write tools are refused at load. The operation must be GET or POST in the pinned document (read from the digested bytes), header parameters may not be Authorization/Host/Cookie/framing names or the auth header, and cookie parameters are unsupported. The tool input_schema mirrors the document's candidate shape: optional path, query, header objects and a body.

What is sent: only parameters the operation declares are sent (the rest are dropped), values with control characters are refused, the URL is the manifest base_url plus the document path (never an input URL; path-parameter values containing / \ or % are refused), and nothing from the inbound MCP request (headers, cookies, connector token) is forwarded. Calls use no proxy, refuse private, loopback and reserved addresses after DNS resolution (load-time checks are syntactic only), refuse every redirect, time out at 30 seconds and cap the response at 4 MiB.

Results: the JSON response must match the operation's declared response schema; only the tool's output.include fields are projected and validated. The result uses the shared envelope with no source_revisions, completeness complete/declared_output and the warning external_source. Failures use the stable codes: unreachable provider, redirect or non-2xx is unavailable_provider; oversize, non-JSON or schema mismatch is incomplete_result; a missing credential, one stored for another host, or a provider 401/403/404 is denied (the message names the connection and the route, never a credential).

Credentials: each user stores their own upstream credential per connection, sealed under the app's ENCRYPTION_KEY and bound to the user, the connection and the upstream host (changing a connection's base_url host makes every stored credential unusable until each user enters it again); it is never returned by any API, tool, audit row or log. GET/PUT/DELETE /api/_mcp/connections/{name}/credential (PUT body {"secret": "..."}, single line, up to 4096 bytes) manage it from a signed-in browser session only: a direct-login cookie session with a CSRF token, never a bearer, API token, scoped, impersonated or act-as session; GET reports only {configured: bool}. A durable ENCRYPTION_KEY is required. Upstream OAuth flows are not supported (bearer and api-key header only). Removing a connection from mcp.yaml (or setting its auth kind to none) deletes every user's credential for it when the manifest loads, so re-adding the same name and host starts empty. `disable --revoke` deletes all of them (`connector_owner_switches`); account deletion, restore and key rotation are in `connector_lifecycle`.

Transfers: selected-file pull and approved artifact push go through manifest-pinned transfer declarations, a readable row/upload binding and the durable effect queue. Transfer declarations use `transfer.kind` (`pull` or `push`), `connection`, and `operation_id`. Pulls use the pinned GET operation: they bind `selector_intent_path` to the pinned `selector_parameter`, decode `content_field`, and check `mime_field` against `expected_mime`, with `revision_field` and `checksum_field` recording source provenance; `attach_tool`, `record_id_intent_path` and `file_column` define the authorized canonical row attachment. Pushes bind `artifact_intent_path` to a reviewed artifact, place standard-base64 encoded verified bytes in `request_content_field`, and send the derived idempotency key in `request_idempotency_field` to the pinned POST operation; `reconcile_operation_id` and `reconcile_parameter` name the pinned GET read-only lookup, while `result_id_field` and `result_checksum_field` verify its result.

Transfer rules: pulls record upstream identity and content provenance; uncertain pushes are reconciled through the pinned upstream read operation instead of blind replay. Reviewed source-file selectors, destination record identifiers and artifact identifiers may be intent inputs only through declared, authorized transfer tools; they are then checked against the pinned connection contract, readable-row/upload binding and content provenance. Names and paths are manifest-reviewed, never provider URLs supplied by the model. Continuous sync and public publication are unsupported; arbitrary model-supplied URLs, guessed provider envelopes, last-write-wins and bypassing the row gate are refused. A transfer receipt seals its payload digest; confirmed `pushed` or `attached` state is durable delivery evidence, while uncertain state remains unknown.

Transfer limits: decoded pull content is capped at 25 MiB. Pushes may reference reviewed artifacts up to 50 MiB; serialized transfer requests and provider responses are capped at 35 MiB, while reconciliation responses use the 4 MiB cap of external reads.
